Your Creative Director

🧠 Blank Page? Hit the Button

🔁 Rebuild in My Voice

✍️ Generate a Full Draft
Brief it, generate it, edit it, post it. Any format, whenever you need it.
💬
Director Chat
Bring over anything you are already working on and ask for it reworked, or open a brand new chat for a different offer, service, or voice entirely. Ask the logistics questions too: when to send something, how often to post, what to prioritize next. It gives you a real answer instead of bouncing the decision back to you.
A real exchange, not a script
how often should I actually be posting on IG, I keep seeing people say daily and I cannot do that
3 to 5 times a week is a real, sustainable floor, not daily. Daily is a ceiling some accounts chase, not a baseline you owe anyone. Consistency at a pace you can actually keep beats a streak that burns you out in three weeks and then goes quiet for a month, which is worse for the algorithm and for you than just posting 4 times a week forever.
📊 Ask the strategy questions
When to post, how often, what to do first, a real answer, not "it depends."
✍️ Rework what you wrote
Paste a draft and ask for it warmer, shorter, or totally different.
💭 Think out loud
It saves automatically and is always there when you come back.

Built for Substack creators
Substack is having a moment, and long-form writing is one of the hardest content formats for ND brains. The Studio is built to change that. Generate full Substack-ready articles in your voice, with a compelling title, opening hook, body sections, and a warm close. Not a bullet list dressed up as an article. The real thing, ready to paste and publish.
📄 Full article generation
Brief your idea, choose Article as your format, and get a complete long-form draft back. Title, hook, sections, close. Written in your voice, ready to edit and post.
✦ Strategy before you write
Run Get Creative Direction on your Substack idea before you draft anything. Get the angle, the emotional frame, and the one thing to avoid.
🪝 Hook your readers from line one
Use the Hook Builder to generate five opening lines for your article before you write a word. Pick the one that pulls. Substack readers decide in the first two sentences whether they are staying.

📖How to use each section
▼
Prefer one long read instead of clicking through each section below? The Complete Studio Guide covers everything here in one place, including a slow, no-pressure 3 month plan if you'd rather ease in than dive in all at once.
🏠Dashboard›

Your home base. A few tools live only here and nowhere else in the Studio, made for quick, low-effort starts rather than deep work.

  • Help me, Creative Director!: the fastest way to get unstuck. One click for instant direction, angle, hook, emotion, what to avoid, no topic required if you don't have one yet.
  • This Week's Focus: 1 to 3 things, no dates, no pressure. A small visible reminder of what actually matters this week, separate from your full task list.
  • What do you want to create today?: quick-pick cards for the most common formats, skip the setup and land straight in a content card or the Studio.
  • Pick up where you left off: your most recent draft and content card, one click back in.
  • Tip: the Getting Started checklist at the top tracks your first few steps in the Studio. Dismiss it anytime, it can be brought back from Settings.
✦Creative Director›

The brain of the Studio. Three ways to use it: the Panic Button on your dashboard for instant direction, Get Creative Direction inside any content card before you write, and Rebuild in my voice for rebuilding posts that stopped your scroll in your own voice.

  • Brief Me: add a topic and hit Brief Me to get a full content direction, angle, hook, emotion, and what to avoid, before you write a single word.
  • Surprise Me: no idea what to post? Hit Surprise Me for a completely random content idea and creative direction generated for you, no topic required.
  • Analog Prompt: not feeling the AI today? Hit Analog Prompt for a writing spark with zero generation. Just a question or nudge to get you thinking. No credits used.
  • Save to Drafts: hit Save Brief to Drafts at any point to save your topic or the full generated brief to your Saved Drafts library.
  • Get Creative Direction: inside any content card, open Bridge the Gap and click Get Creative Direction before you write.
  • Rebuild in my voice: paste any post you saw anywhere and the Creative Director rebuilds it in your voice for your audience.
  • Tip: fill in your Brand Profile in Settings first. Every output uses it automatically so you never have to re-explain your niche.
✍️Writing Studio›

Write your own content or generate with AI. Both approaches save to your draft library. The writing area is front and centre. AI tools are there when you want them, out of the way when you do not.

  • Go Analog: open the Studio and just write. The right panel is a clean writing area with no AI in sight. Title, subtitle, writing area, tags, links. That is it.
  • Bridge the Gap: click AI Tools in the header to open the left panel when you want generation help. It is hidden by default so you never feel pressured to use it.
  • Instructions field: in the AI panel, tell it exactly what you want before generating. Keep my voice, punch up the hook, make it shorter. It will follow it.
  • Use my draft: check the box in the AI panel to have the AI work from what you have already written rather than starting from scratch.
  • Articles and Substack: the AI automatically generates a title and subtitle and places them in the fields above your draft. You do not need to write them yourself.
  • Analog badge: drafts you write yourself get an Analog badge in Saved Drafts. Filter by Analog Only anytime to see exactly what is yours.
  • Saved Drafts: everything you save goes to Saved Drafts in the sidebar. Filter by platform, analog only, or AI-assisted. Exportable as CSV anytime.
💬Director Chat›

An open chat with your Creative Director, and your strategist. Use it to rework anything you're already creating in the Studio, open a fresh chat for a different business or voice, or ask the logistics questions, like when to send something or how often to post.

  • Ask it the strategy questions: when to send a newsletter, how often to post, what to prioritize this week. Set up your Strategy & Logistics profile in Settings so it knows your platforms, cadence, timezone, and goal.
  • Rework what you're already writing: bring a draft over from the Writing Studio or a content card and ask for it warmer, more direct, or a totally different angle.
  • Switch voices on the fly: paste any copy and tell it which business or tone to write in. No need to set up a separate brand profile first.
  • Think out loud: talk through an idea before you commit it to a content card or draft.
  • It remembers, every conversation: click History to see every past chat, switch back to any of them, or delete the ones you don't need. Starting a New Chat never deletes the old one.
  • Export anytime: click Export to copy the whole chat or download it as a text file to keep.
📌Repurposed File›

Your personal reference library for the best AI outputs you generate. Find it under Library in the sidebar.

  • How to save: after running a Rebuild in my voice, click the Save to Repurposed File button to store the rebuilt post permanently.
  • How to use it: open Library, then Repurposed File. Search by platform or content, expand full text, copy, or view the original autopsy analysis.
  • Tip: save your best angles here so you can come back to them when you hit a creative block instead of starting from scratch.
📋Content Planner›

Your visual kanban board for tracking every piece of content from first idea to published. Each card holds your brief, AI tools, tasks, images, and status all in one place.

  • Ideas column: dump anything here. Half-formed thoughts count. Just get it out of your head.
  • In Progress: move it here when you have started writing or designing.
  • Ready to Post: caption written, graphic done, waiting to go live.
  • Published: move it here once it is live so you can see your output at a glance.
  • Go Analog in cards: every content card opens with the Go Analog section expanded. Write your own draft, hook, or notes directly in the card with no AI required.
  • Bridge the Gap in cards: click Bridge the Gap inside any card to open the AI tools: Get Creative Direction, Generate Content, Hook Builder, Caption Variations, Rebuild in my voice.
  • This Week's Focus: use the checklist on your dashboard to pick 1-3 things to work on this week. No dates, no pressure.
  • Tip: open a card and run Get Creative Direction or Generate Content without ever leaving the Planner.
✅Tasks›

A kanban board for everything that is not content. Business tasks, admin, client work, launch to-dos. Energy level tags and time estimates make it ND-friendly by design.

  • Energy tags: label each task High, Medium, or Low energy. On a low-energy day, filter to low-energy tasks only and protect yourself.
  • Time estimates: add how long something will actually take. Be honest. This helps you build realistic calendar blocks.
  • Substeps: break any task into smaller actions so your brain always knows what the next physical step is.
  • Tip: start each week by picking 3 tasks that will actually move the needle. Not the most urgent, the most impactful.
📅Calendar›

Map out your content and tasks on one calendar. Click Add Entry to choose between adding a content entry or a task. Color-coded so you always know what you are looking at.

  • Content entries: map out when content goes live. Rust dots for content, teal for tasks.
  • Add Entry picker: clicking Add Entry gives you the choice to add content or a task so nothing ends up in the wrong place.
  • Tip: map out next week every Friday. Even rough placeholder entries give your brain a container for the week ahead.
🔗Library›

Four pre-built libraries plus your personal Repurposed File. Hooks, CTAs, Story Ideas, Writing Prompts, and everything you save from the Studio.

  • Hooks: scroll-stopping opening lines. Copy one into your brief or caption as a starting point.
  • CTAs: end every post with a clear call to action. Pick the one that matches your goal for that piece.
  • Story Ideas: for when you open Instagram with no idea what to post to your Stories.
  • Prompts: writing prompts for the Studio. Copy and fill in the brackets with your specifics.
  • Repurposed File: your saved Rebuild in my voice rebuilds. Search, expand, copy, or remove anytime.
  • Tip: bookmark your favourites by clicking the heart so you can find them again quickly.
🖼️Feed Preview›

See your Instagram grid before you post. Any Instagram content card with an uploaded image shows up here as a live grid you can drag to rearrange.

  • Add images: open any Instagram content card, scroll to the image section, and upload your photo or graphic.
  • Drag to rearrange: drag tiles around to see how different sequences look before you commit to posting.
  • Tip: use this before a batch session to check your grid has visual variety. Mix graphics, photos, and text tiles so it does not look repetitive.
🧠Notebooks›

Unlimited notebooks for anything that does not fit anywhere else. Thoughts, ideas, client notes, brain dumps. No wrong way to use it.

  • Brain Dump mode: when your head is full, open a notebook and just type. No editing, no organizing. Get it out first, sort it later.
  • Content parking lot: ideas that are not ready for the Planner yet. Keep them here until you have bandwidth.
  • Tip: review your notebooks weekly and move anything that is ready into the Content Planner.
📖Guides›

Built-in strategy playbooks written for neurodivergent entrepreneurs. Find them under Think in the sidebar, or use the guide cards at the top of your dashboard to jump straight in.

  • Big Brain Energy (Strategy Edition): how to actually use Director Chat as your strategist, what to ask it, how to set up your logistics profile, and how to start leaning into strategy without it feeling intimidating.
  • ND Rescue Kit: what to do when you are overwhelmed and do not know where to start. Four-step reset, ND-friendly batching, launch planning, and how to use every Studio tool to reduce content stress.
  • Content Cycle Framework: a four-phase content rhythm that grows your audience, nurtures your community, converts the right people, and gives you space to breathe. Includes a full four-week example calendar.
  • The Unstuck Guide: for when your inner critic says it has all been done before. Reframes for perfectionism and starting paralysis, paired with specific Studio workflows to get you moving again.
  • The Analog Way: no AI required. What analog means, why it is having a moment, how to use the Studio as a fully analog creator, and 15 writing prompts to spark content from your own experience.
  • The IG Resurrection Guide: a gentle, practical plan for posting again after a ghosted or quiet account. Covers content and posting, engagement and the algorithm, SEO over hashtags, why community matters more than reach, and a low-overwhelm way to actually begin.
  • Dashboard carousel: the guide cards at the top of your dashboard link directly to each guide so you never have to hunt for them.
  • Tip: if a strategy question is stressing you out, open Big Brain Energy. If you are overwhelmed, open the ND Rescue Kit. If you are not sure about AI, open The Analog Way. If your account has gone quiet, open The IG Resurrection Guide. Each one exists for exactly that moment.

How the Studio is laid out
🏠
Dashboard
Your home base. Brain not cooperating, This Week's Focus, quick-create buttons, Pick Up Where You Left Off, and On Your Plate. If the rest of the Studio ever feels like too much on a given day, this page alone is enough to work from.

Go Analog, the short version
Every content card has two halves: Go Analog and Bridge the Gap. Go Analog is where you write it yourself, no AI required, a Hook/Subject field, a Caption/Body field, and a place for your own draft. It's open by default every time, because this Studio was built to default to you, not to AI.
✏️
Want the full picture?
This is the short version. For what analog actually means, why it's having a moment, and how to use every corner of the Studio without touching AI at all, read The Analog Way guide.
Every AI tool, and what it actually gives you
✦
Get Creative Direction
This does not write your post. It gives you the angle, the hook idea, the emotion to aim for, and what to avoid, based on your brief. Direction, not a finished draft.

Try this: you know you want to post about a client win but not how to frame it. Type "client win, went from posting randomly to having a real content system" into the brief, hit Get Creative Direction, and use what comes back as your outline before you write a word.
✍️
Generate Content
This is the one that writes the finished piece. Pick a format, Caption, Story, Carousel, Reel Script, Newsletter, Email, or Substack Article, and it builds the whole thing, shaped correctly for that format.

Try this: you have a topic but no time to write today. Fill in the Notes field with 2-3 bullet points of what you want covered, pick Carousel, hit Generate. You'll get labeled, ready-to-edit slides back, not a wall of text you have to break apart yourself.
🪝
Hook Builder
Gives you 5 real hook options built from your brief. Pick the one that sounds like you, then build the full post out from it in one more click.

Try this: you've written a full caption but the first line feels flat. Open Hook Builder on that same card, get 5 options, swap in whichever one actually stops a scroll, keep the rest of your caption as is.
⇕
Caption Variations
Same idea, 3 different angles. Useful when you're not sure which direction fits best.

Try this: a launch caption is high stakes and you don't want to commit to the first draft. Generate variations, read all 3 out loud, post whichever one actually sounds like you'd say it to a friend.
☆
Content Series
A real, connected 5-part series built from your voice and niche, not five random unrelated posts.

Try this: you have a launch coming up and one hyperfocus afternoon to prep for it. Use Content Series once instead of writing 5 separate captions from scratch, you'll get a week's worth of connected posts to edit and schedule instead of five blank pages.
🔁
Rebuild in My Voice
Paste in a post you admire. This breaks down why it works, then rebuilds something 100% original in your own voice. Not a rewrite, a completely new piece that learned from good bones.

Try this: you screenshotted a post months ago and never touched it because you didn't want to copy it. Paste the text into Rebuild in My Voice, get an analysis of why it worked, then a brand new version built for your niche.
Getting the most out of Director Chat
🧭
Settings → Strategy & Logistics
This is what turns Director Chat from a writing assistant into an actual strategist. It's a separate section from your Brand Profile, five fields: Primary Platforms, Posting Frequency, Audience Timezone, Current Phase/Goal, and an optional What's Worked Before note. Fill it out once and questions like "when should I post this" or "how often should I be showing up on Instagram" get a real, specific answer instead of Director Chat bouncing the question back to you. If you never touch it, Director Chat will still help, it'll just default to general best practice instead of your actual situation.

Try this: add "mostly US Eastern" to Audience Timezone and "launching a new offer this month" to Current Phase/Goal, then ask Director Chat "what should I post this week?" The answer will be shaped around that goal and timezone instead of being generic.
The dashboard tools
🧠
Creative Director Mode (Brain Not Cooperating)
Three ways out of a blank brain. Brief Me gives you direction using a topic you already have. Surprise Me does the same but also hands you a fresh idea, no topic needed. Analog Prompt is a no-AI writing prompt, zero credits used. There's also a Write the Full Piece option if you want the finished draft directly from here instead of a content card.

Director Chat

Your Brand Profile matters more than it seems
🎨
Settings → Brand Profile
Every AI tool in this Studio pulls from your Brand Profile, your niche, your ideal client, your voice, your offers, what's worked before. An empty profile means the AI is working with almost nothing to go on, and the output will feel more generic because of it. Five minutes filling this out is the single biggest thing you can do to make every tool in here sound more like you.
How credits work on your account
✦
One credit per AI generation, nothing else costs anything
Every time you click a button that generates something with AI, Get Creative Direction, Generate Content, Hook Builder, Caption Variations, Content Series, Rebuild in My Voice, Brief Me, Surprise Me, Write the Full Piece, or sending a message in Director Chat, that's one credit. That's the whole list. Browsing the Studio, planning in the Content Planner, writing your own content in Go Analog, using Notebooks, moving tasks around, none of it touches your credits, ever. Analog Prompt on the dashboard also does not use a credit, since it's not AI at all.

Starter includes 100 credits a month, Unlimited means exactly that, no cap. Either way, credits reset at the start of each new month, they don't roll over, and you can see exactly how many you've used and how many are left any time from the "Studio in Session" bar in your sidebar.
If you'd rather take this slow, a 3 month plan
This is optional. You can use the whole Studio on day one if that feels good to you. But if a brand new tool with this many parts feels like a lot right now, here's a slower way in. No deadlines, no falling behind, just a rough shape to lean on if you want one. Go slower than this if you need to. That's still doing it right.
Month 1: Just the Dashboard
Log in. Look at This Week's Focus, pick 1 to 3 things, no dates attached. If you write anything, use Go Analog on a content card, no AI needed yet. When you're stuck, hit the Analog Prompt button on the dashboard, still no AI. That's genuinely enough for a whole month. You're building the habit of opening the Studio, not mastering every feature.

Concretely: weeks 1-2, just add your 1-3 focus items and open the app most days. Weeks 3-4, write one piece of content fully analog, start to finish, no AI tools touched at all.
Month 2: One AI tool at a time
Fill out your Brand Profile and Strategy & Logistics whenever you have ten quiet minutes, this makes everything after it better. Then try one AI tool a week. You don't need to use all of them. You're finding out which ones actually help you, not checking a box.

Concretely: week 1, fill out Brand Profile and Strategy & Logistics in Settings. Week 2, try Get Creative Direction on your next content card. Week 3, try Hook Builder on a caption you've already drafted. Week 4, ask Director Chat one real question about your posting schedule.
Month 3: Build your own rhythm
By now you probably know which tools you reach for and which ones you don't, and that's the point, there's no wrong combination. Maybe you live in the Content Planner. Maybe Director Chat became your favorite. Start using whatever that rhythm is for real content, on your actual schedule, at your actual pace.

Concretely: pick 2-3 tools from Month 2 that actually felt useful and build them into how you already work, drop the rest. If nothing from Month 2 clicked yet, that's fine too, stay analog and revisit AI tools whenever you're curious, there's no clock running on this.
💛
One last thing
There is no version of this where you're doing it wrong. Use one tool or use all of them. Go fast some weeks and slow on others. This Studio was built to bend around you, not the other way around.

ND Rescue Kit
You're overwhelmed. That's okay. Here's what to do right now.
This isn't a 10-step productivity system. It's a reset. When your brain is full and your to-do list feels like it's staring at you, this is the starting point. We'll get you to one small, clear next action, and that's enough.
The four-step reset
🧠
Step 1: Brain dump first, plan second
Before you do anything else, open Notebooks and do a Brain Dump session. Get everything out of your head and into the Studio. It doesn't need to be organized. Just write. The goal is to stop holding all of it in your working memory.
🎯
Step 2: Pick ONE thing
When the brain dump is done, look at what you wrote and pick the single thing that would create the most relief if it was finished. Not the most urgent, not the most impressive. The one that would make you breathe easier. That's your next action.
⚡
Step 3: Match to your energy level
Before you open a task, check in. Are you high energy, medium energy, or running on fumes? Your Task Board has energy tags for a reason. On low days, only do low-energy tasks. Protecting your energy is not laziness, it's how you stay consistent long-term.
⏱
Step 4: Time block for your brain
ND brains do better with shorter, protected work blocks than long open-ended sessions. Try 25 minutes on, 10 minutes off. Add your task to the Calendar with a realistic time estimate. When the block ends, stop, even if you're not finished. Stopping on time builds trust with yourself.
How to use the Studio to reduce content overwhelm
✦
Hit the panic button
When you have absolutely no idea what to post, the Creative Director button on your dashboard generates a full content direction instantly. Platform, format, hook angle, emotion to create, what to avoid. You go from blank page to brief in under a minute.
🗂
Keep ideas in the Planner, not in your head
Every time a content idea hits you, add it to the Content Planner as an Idea. Don't think about it yet. Just capture it. When you sit down to actually create, you'll already have a list to pull from instead of staring at a blank page.
✍️
Use the Writing Studio to start, not to finish
The AI draft is not a finished post. It's a starting point that breaks the blank page paralysis. Generate the draft, edit what doesn't feel like you, and publish. Most of your thinking happens in the editing, not the generating.
🪝
Start with a hook, not a caption
The Hook Builder is your secret weapon for starting. When you don't know how to open a post, generate five hooks for your idea, pick the one that clicks, and write from there. The hook is the hardest part. Once that's done, the rest comes easier.
📅
Put it on the calendar before you make it
Mapping out content before it exists creates gentle accountability without pressure. Add a calendar entry for the post, even if it's just an idea. Seeing it on the calendar gives your brain a container for the work instead of a floating obligation.
Batching your content the ND way
Batch Strategy
Do one thing many times, not many things once
Batching is not about spending eight hours creating content on a Sunday. That's a burnout setup. ND-friendly batching means picking one task type and doing a focused burst of just that. Ideas only. Hooks only. Drafts only. Scheduling only. Switching between modes is where the energy drain happens.
💡
Batch 1: Idea capture (15 min)
Open the Content Planner. Set a 15-minute timer. Brain dump every content idea you have, no judging, no developing. Just capture. You're filling the pipeline, not building content yet.
🪝
Batch 2: Hook generation (20 min)
Pick your top 5 ideas from the Planner. Open each card and run the Hook Builder. Choose your favourite hook for each. Now you have 5 posts with strong openings ready to develop.
✍️
Batch 3: Draft generation (30 min)
Take your hooked ideas into the Writing Studio. Generate drafts for each one. Edit, adjust tone, make it yours. Move each card to Draft in the Planner when it's done.
📅
Batch 4: Map it out (10 min)
Add your drafts to the Calendar with target publish dates. Move cards to Scheduled in the Planner. You're done. A week of content mapped out without a single marathon session.
Planning a launch without the spiral
🗓
Set your launch date first
Add your launch date to the Calendar. Then work backwards. If you're launching in 4 weeks, plan content for weeks 1, 2, 3, and launch week. Put each phase on the calendar now, even roughly.
📋
Use Tasks for the non-content work
Sales page, email sequence, checkout link, graphics. These live in your Task Board. Break each one into substeps with time estimates and energy tags. Assign them to calendar blocks so nothing gets left to the last minute.
🔄
Pre-load a Content Series
Use the Content Series Builder on your launch topic to generate 5 connected posts. These become your launch content runway. One idea, five pieces of content, done in one session.
🎯
Know your one CTA before you start
Every piece of launch content should point to one place. Decide your single call to action before you write anything. Browse the CTA Library if you need starting points. A clear CTA makes writing every post faster.
Six principles for making this stick
  • ✦
    Your system only works if it's frictionless enough to actually use. If something in the Studio feels like too many steps, skip it. The best workflow is the one you'll actually do.
  • ◎
    Consistency beats perfection every time. Three posts a week published reliably beats 10 posts planned and none posted. Set a pace you can hold on your worst week, not your best.
  • ✶
    Use Caption Variations when you're stuck on tone. If the draft doesn't sound like you, generate three variations and see which one clicks. Sometimes you need to see options before you know what feels right.
  • ✦
    Add the Studio to your home screen. Reducing the steps between idea and capture is how you actually capture ideas. The fewer clicks, the more ideas make it in.
  • ◎
    Review your Content Planner once a week, not every day. Pick one day to move cards, check what's scheduled, and plan the coming week. That one session is your whole planning practice.
  • ✶
    Done is the standard, not polished. Published content that's 80% great reaches people. Perfect content sitting in Drafts reaches no one.

Content Cycle Framework
Your content is supposed to ebb and flow, not sprint forever.
Most content advice treats every week the same. But sustainable content creation has a rhythm, like a tide. Grow, nurture, convert, reflect. Each phase serves your audience differently, and together they build a business that doesn't require you to be always on.
The four phases
01
Grow
Reach new people with content that travels beyond your current followers
Audience growth
02
Nurture
Pour into your existing audience, build trust and deepen the relationship
Retention + trust
03
Convert
Make offers, invite people in, and move the right ones toward working with you
Sales + enrollment
04
Reflect
Slow down, share behind the scenes, and reconnect with why you do this work
Community + renewal
How long is each phase?
One week per phase is the default, making it a clean four-week cycle. But if a phase is working, stay in it. Nurture weeks can run two to three weeks when your audience engagement is high. Convert phases can be shorter if your offer is time-limited. The cycle is a guide, not a rule.
Phase 01: Grow
What to create
Content that travels beyond your current followers
Shareable takes on common problems in your niche. Educational posts that answer a question your ideal client is searching. Relatable observations that make people tag a friend. Opinion posts that spark conversation and shares. Your goal: be found by people who don't know you yet.
Studio tools to use
Hook Builder + Content Series
Run the Hook Builder on your grow-phase ideas to find the most shareable angles. Use the Content Series Builder to turn one strong concept into five posts that cover it from multiple entry points, each one a door for a new follower to find you.
Phase 02: Nurture
What to create
Content that deepens trust with people already following you
Behind-the-scenes of your process or thinking. Personal stories that reveal your values and perspective. Client wins and transformation stories, with permission. Lessons you've learned the hard way. Answers to questions your audience actually asks you. Your goal: make your existing audience feel seen, supported, and glad they followed you.
Studio tools to use
Writing Studio + Notebooks
Use your Notebooks to brain dump stories and reflections, then bring the best ones into the Writing Studio for a newsletter or long-form post. Caption Variations is useful here too: try the warm and story-led versions of your drafts to find the nurture tone.
Phase 03: Convert
What to create
Content that creates clarity around your offer and moves people to act
Posts that name the specific problem your offer solves. Addressing common objections directly and honestly. What's included, what it costs, and who it's for. Testimonials and results, real ones. A clear and direct call to action on every post. Your goal: make it easy for the right people to say yes.
Studio tools to use
Rebuild in my voice + CTA Library
Paste top-performing sales content from others into the Rebuild in my voice to understand why it worked, then rebuild it in your voice. Browse the CTA Library for convert-phase endings that feel natural, not pushy. Run the Get Creative Direction on your offer to get a directional angle before you write.
Phase 04: Reflect
What to create
Content that reconnects you and your audience to meaning and community
Monthly or seasonal recaps of what you're noticing, learning, or building. Gratitude posts that name your community specifically. Behind-the-scenes of your life or creative process, the parts that aren't polished. Questions that invite your audience to share their experience. Your goal: show up as a human, not a content machine.
Studio tools to use
Notebooks + Brain Dump
The reflect phase is the right time to do a Brain Dump session in Notebooks. Empty everything out about the last cycle: what worked, what felt hard, what you want more of. This becomes the raw material for your next grow phase. Reflection feeds the cycle forward.
What a four-week cycle looks like in practice
Week 1: Grow
Mon
Educational post: common myth in your niche
Teach
Tue
Shareable take or unpopular opinion
Opinion
Wed
Answer a question new followers commonly ask
FAQ
Thu
Relatable moment that makes people tag a friend
Relatable
Fri
Value drop: quick tip they can use today
Value
Week 2: Nurture
Mon
A lesson you learned the hard way
Story
Tue
Client transformation story, with permission
Proof
Wed
Behind-the-scenes of how you work or think
BTS
Thu
Your actual values or beliefs about your niche
Values
Fri
Ask your audience a question that invites them in
Engage
Week 3: Convert
Mon
Name the problem your offer solves specifically
Problem
Tue
Address the top objection your ideal client has
Objection
Wed
What's included, who it's for, what it costs
Offer
Thu
A real result or testimonial with context
Proof

CTA
Week 4: Reflect
Mon
What you noticed or learned this month
Reflect

Sneak peek
Fri
Gratitude or community shoutout post
Community
Making the cycle work for an ND brain
  • ✦
    You don't need 5 posts a week. This framework works with 3, 2, or even 1 post a week. The ratio of phase types matters more than the volume.
  • ◎
    Batch your content by phase, not by week. At the start of a grow phase, batch all your grow posts in one session. Your brain stays in the same mode the whole time, which is much easier than switching between grow and convert thinking every other post.
  • ✶
    Use the Content Planner to tag your cycle phase. Add the phase name to the notes field of each content card. When you look at your Planner, you can immediately see if you're missing a phase or over-indexing on one type.
  • ✦
    Let the reflect phase be genuinely lighter. Fewer posts, more presence. The reflect phase is designed to give you breathing room. Protect this week so the next grow phase can launch from a full tank.
  • ◎
    The cycle compounds over time. Month one, you're building the habit. Month three, you're building trust. Month six, people know your rhythm and show up for it. Consistency with this framework over six months is more powerful than any single viral post.

The Unstuck Guide
It has been done before. Do it anyway.
The inner critic that says your idea isn't original enough, your niche is too crowded, or someone already said it better is not telling you the truth. It's telling you it's scared. This guide is about learning to tell the difference, then creating anyway.
The reframe first
Everything has been done before. That's not the point.
There are thousands of fitness coaches, therapists, copywriters, photographers, and healers online. People still choose one over another. They choose based on voice, on resonance, on the specific way someone explains a thing. Your job is not to be the first person to talk about your topic. Your job is to be the person your specific audience hears it from. Nobody else has your combination of experience, perspective, and way of putting things. That's not a small thing. That's the whole thing.
🧠
What the inner critic is actually doing
The "it's been done" thought is a protection mechanism, not an assessment of quality. Your brain is trying to keep you from the risk of being seen and judged. Recognizing it as fear rather than fact is the first move. You don't argue with it. You notice it, name it, and create anyway.
🔁
Originality is a remix, not an invention
Every creator you admire is remixing influences, experiences, and ideas they absorbed from somewhere else. The question isn't whether your idea is new. It's whether your take on it is honest and specific to you. Specific always beats generic. Personal always beats polished.
When you can't start: the practical moves
✦
The Studio move for this
Open the Content Planner, create a card, and fill in just the brief field with whatever half-formed thought is stuck in your head. Don't judge it. Don't develop it yet. Then run Get Creative Direction. Let the Creative Director give you an angle before you decide if the idea is worth anything. Most ideas look better once they have a direction.
⏱
The two-minute start rule
When you can't begin, the goal is not to write a good post. The goal is to write for two minutes without stopping. Open the Writing Studio, set a mental timer, and type whatever comes out. No editing, no deleting. Two minutes of movement breaks the freeze more reliably than waiting until you feel ready.
🪝
Start with what bothers you, not what inspires you
When inspiration isn't there, frustration usually is. What's a piece of advice in your industry you disagree with? What do clients always get wrong before they come to you? What would you say to your past self? Contrarian and honest beats inspired and generic every time. Use the Hook Builder to turn that frustration into an opening line.
📌
Steal from your own past work
Open your Repurposed File or Saved Drafts. Find something you wrote that felt right at the time. Run Caption Variations on it. Build a Content Series from the core idea. Your best thinking from six months ago is invisible to someone discovering you today. Nothing is too old to revisit.
🔍
Learn from what already works
Find a post that stopped your scroll, from anyone in any niche, and paste it into the Rebuild in my voice. Let the Creative Director break down why it worked, then rebuild the structure in your voice with your topic. You're not copying. You're learning from signal and applying it honestly.
When perfectionism is the block
The reframe
Perfectionism isn't high standards. It's fear with better branding.
High standards produce work and refine it. Perfectionism produces nothing and calls that careful. The difference is whether the standard is serving the work or protecting you from the moment of publishing. If you've been editing the same draft for three days, it's probably done. What you're doing now is stalling.
✂️
The 80% rule
Set a personal policy: when a draft is 80% of where you want it, it ships. The last 20% almost never changes how it lands for the reader, but it costs you hours and keeps you in your head. 80% published beats 100% sitting in Drafts every single time.
📤
Use the friction of publishing as a deadline
Put the post on your Calendar with today's date. Add a task with a time estimate of 10 minutes for final edits. When the time is up, it goes. Externalizing the deadline moves the decision out of your head and into your system, where your ND brain can actually work with it.
When you start strong and then abandon it
💡
Capture the energy, not the finished thing
When an idea hits with force, your job in that moment is not to finish it. It's to capture the core of it before the energy fades. Open a Notebook, dump the raw idea, the feeling, the angle. Even two sentences. The draft can come later. The spark is what to protect.
🗂
Turn abandoned drafts into new starts
Go to your Saved Drafts. Find something you left half-finished. Paste the opening paragraph into the Writing Studio as your starting point and generate from there. Or run Caption Variations on just the hook. Abandoned work is not wasted. It's pre-work for the next version of the same idea.
Six things to remember when you're stuck
  • ✦
    The thought "someone already said this" is almost always fear, not fact. Someone has. Your audience hasn't heard it from you yet, and that's the part that matters.
  • ◎
    You don't need a new idea. You need a new angle on an existing one. Run Get Creative Direction on something you've already posted. The Creative Director will find an angle you haven't used yet.
  • ✶
    Movement beats motivation. You won't feel like creating before you start. The feeling comes after. Open the app first. Wait for inspiration after.
  • ✦
    Your Notebooks are full of content you've already written. Open them before you decide you have nothing to say. Half your best ideas are already there, unfinished and waiting.
  • ◎
    Specificity is the cure for feeling generic. Any time a draft feels too bland, make one detail more specific. A real person, a real moment, a real number. Specificity is what makes people feel seen.
  • ✶
    Finishing something imperfect is an act of self-respect. You are allowed to put things into the world that aren't your best work. Consistency builds trust. Occasional brilliance doesn't.
← Back to Guides
✏️
The Analog Way
You don't have to use AI to use this Studio.
Flow State Studio was built by someone who was done apologizing for how her brain works. That means it was built to hold all kinds of brains, including the ones that think better with a pen, a prompt, and space to breathe. This guide is for you.
What analog actually means right now
Analog is not anti-technology. It's pro-thinking.
Analog is trending right now because a lot of people, especially creative and neurodivergent people, are realizing that AI can speed things up but it can't replace the thinking that makes content actually mean something. Analog means starting from yourself. Your experience, your observations, your honest take on your niche. It's the part that no tool can generate because it comes from living the thing you're talking about.
📈
Why it's having a moment
Audiences are getting good at spotting AI-generated content. The posts that stop the scroll right now are the ones that feel human, specific, and a little imperfect. Personal stories. Honest opinions. Observations that only someone who's actually lived it could write. That's analog. And it's not going anywhere.
🧠
Why it works for ND creators specifically
ND brains often think in associations, tangents, and unexpected connections. That's not a liability. That's exactly what makes analog content interesting. When you write from your own experience without editing yourself before you start, what comes out is specific, real, and resonant in a way that templated content almost never is.
How to use the Studio fully analog
✏️
Go Analog is always open by default
Every content card opens with the Go Analog section expanded and the Bridge the Gap AI tools collapsed. That is intentional. The Studio defaults to you. Open Bridge the Gap only when and if you want to.
📋
Content Planner, analog style
Use the Planner exactly as it is. Add your ideas as cards, track them from Idea to Published, and write your content directly in the Go Analog textarea. Nothing in the Planner requires AI. The kanban board, the calendar entries, the status tracking, all of it works without touching a single AI tool.
✍️
Writing Studio, analog style
Open Writing Studio and ignore the AI Tools button entirely. The right panel is a clean, open writing area. Add your title, your subtitle if you have one, and write. Hit Save to Drafts when you're done. The AI panel is there if you ever want it. It will not force itself on you.
🧠
Notebooks for your raw thinking
Notebooks are the most analog part of the Studio. No AI, no prompts, no structure required. Open a notebook when you need to think out loud, brain dump, or capture something before it disappears. This is where your best content ideas tend to come from, and it is entirely yours.
✏️
Analog Prompt on the dashboard
Open the Creative Director on your dashboard and hit Analog Prompt instead of Brief Me or Surprise Me. You get a writing prompt with zero AI generation. Just a question or a nudge to get you thinking. No credits used, no output generated. Just a spark.
15 analog writing prompts
These are the same prompts in the Analog Prompt button. Use them here as journaling starters, content sparks, or just something to think about. None of them require AI. They just require you.
What is one thing you wish someone had told you when you first started your business?
Describe a moment this week that made you remember why you do this work.
What is the question your ideal client asks most often, and what is your honest answer?
Write about a time something went wrong in your business and what you actually learned from it.
What does a good day in your business actually look like? Be specific.
What is a belief about your industry that you disagree with? Say it plainly.
Who is one person your work has genuinely helped? What changed for them?
What is something you figured out the hard way that your audience needs to hear?
Describe your ideal client not by their job title but by how they feel before they find you.
What would you create if you knew it would not be judged?
What part of your work feels effortless to you that feels impossible to others?
Write the post you have been avoiding writing. Start with why you have been avoiding it.
What does sustainability actually look like in your business right now, not the polished version?
What is one small thing you do differently from everyone else in your niche?
Write a letter to yourself from six months ago about where you are now.
Six things to know as an analog creator here
  • ✦
    You never have to open Bridge the Gap. The Studio works completely without it. Everything that requires AI is clearly labelled and always opt-in.
  • ◎
    Your analog drafts get their own badge. In Saved Drafts, anything you wrote yourself shows an Analog badge. Filter by Analog Only anytime to see exactly what is yours.
  • ✶
    The Notebooks are yours completely. No AI reads your notebooks unless you explicitly copy something into a content card or the Writing Studio. What's in your notebooks stays in your notebooks.
  • ✦
    Analog content and AI content can coexist in the same system. You don't have to choose one mode forever. Some content comes from you entirely. Some days you want a spark. Both are fine. The Studio holds both without making you feel like one is more legitimate than the other.
  • ◎
    Your voice is the point. Whether you write every word yourself or use AI to start and then rewrite everything, the goal is content that sounds like you. The tool doesn't matter. The voice does.
  • ✶
    Done and authentic beats perfect and generated every time. The most powerful content you will ever make is the stuff only you could write. Keep the Analog Prompts close for when you need a way in.

🌱
The IG Resurrection Guide
Your account isn't dead. It's just resting.
A ghosted Instagram doesn't mean you failed. It usually means life happened, your brain needed a break, or the pressure to perform got bigger than the desire to post. This guide is for coming back without the shame spiral, the fear of "starting over," or the overwhelm of not knowing where to even click first. Slow and honest beats loud and burnt out.
Before you post anything, read this
Nobody is keeping score except you.
The fear of coming back usually sounds like: people will notice I disappeared, my old content looks dated now, I have to explain where I went. Almost none of that is true in practice. Most followers didn't notice the gap the way you did, because they weren't watching your account the way you were. The algorithm doesn't remember you were gone and hold it against you. It just looks at what you post now. You don't owe anyone an explanation, a comeback story, or a highlight reel. You just owe yourself a low-pressure way back in.
👻
Going quiet is not the same as starting over
Your account keeps its history, your followers, and your past content whether you posted yesterday or eight months ago. You are not starting from zero. You are picking back up. That distinction matters more than it sounds like it should, because "starting over" carries way more pressure than "picking back up."
🧠
The shame spiral is the actual blocker, not the algorithm
Most ND creators who go quiet aren't stuck because they don't know what to post. They're stuck because the longer the gap gets, the more it feels like a thing that needs to be addressed before they're "allowed" to post again. It doesn't. You can just post. The gap does not need a eulogy.
The first week back: content and posting
🌱
The Studio move for this
Open Director Chat and tell it you're coming back after a quiet stretch and want a few low-pressure post ideas to ease back in, not a big relaunch. Or open the Content Planner, drop a half-formed idea into a card, and run Get Creative Direction before you write a single word.
1️⃣
Post the gap, briefly, then move on
One short, honest line acknowledging you've been quiet does more good than ignoring it or over-explaining it. "Took a break, I'm back, here's what's on my mind" is enough. One sentence, not a paragraph. Then go straight into actual content. The apology tour is optional and usually unnecessary.
2️⃣
Pick the easiest format first, not the best one
Your first post back should be whatever takes the least effort to make, not whatever performs best. A single photo with a caption. A simple Story. The goal of post one is just to post. Save the polished carousel for week three, once momentum exists again.
3️⃣
Three posts in the first week, not seven
A realistic restart is three posts across a week: one feed post, one Story, one piece of light engagement (commenting on others, replying to DMs). That's a comeback. It does not need to look like you never left.
📋
Use the Planner to make the decision once
Pick your three posts for the week in one sitting and drop them into the Content Planner. Deciding what to post every single day is exhausting. Deciding once, for the whole week, removes the daily friction that often causes another quiet stretch.
Engagement and the algorithm, without the hustle culture
The reframe
The algorithm rewards consistency of showing up, not constant posting.
Instagram's systems are looking for signals that you're an active account worth showing to people: posting regularly even if it's not daily, replying to comments and DMs, watching and engaging with content in your niche, and people spending real time on what you share. None of that requires posting every day or chasing trends that don't fit you. It requires being present in a way that's sustainable for you specifically.
💬
Engagement is a two-way habit, not a broadcast
Spend 10 minutes before or after you post replying to comments, answering DMs, and commenting genuinely on a few accounts in your space. This does more for how the algorithm treats your account than almost anything else, and it costs less energy than making another piece of content.
⏱
Reply within the first hour when you can
Early engagement on a post tells the algorithm it's worth showing to more people. You don't need to be glued to your phone, but if you can check in once shortly after posting and reply to early comments, it gives that post a better chance without any extra content creation.
🔁
Consistency beats frequency
Posting twice a week for two months reliably will outperform posting daily for a week and then disappearing again. Pick a rhythm you can actually sustain on a hard week, not your best-case-scenario rhythm. Realistic and repeated wins over ambitious and abandoned.
🚫
You do not have to be everywhere
You don't need Reels, Stories, carousels, and a newsletter all running at once to "be consistent." Pick one or two formats that don't drain you and let the rest be occasional. Showing up exhausted everywhere is worse for your account, and for you, than showing up steadily in one place.
SEO over hashtags
Hashtags are a 2018 strategy. Searchable captions are the current one.
Instagram now functions a lot like a search engine. People type what they're looking for into the search bar the same way they would on Google. That means the words you actually use in your caption, your alt text, and your profile matter more than a wall of hashtags ever did. A handful of relevant hashtags is still fine. They are no longer the main lever.
🔎
Write captions like someone is searching for them
Use the actual words your ideal audience would type into the search bar: your niche, your service, the problem you solve, the city you're in if it's relevant. "ND-friendly business coach for overwhelmed freelancers" gets found. Clever wordplay with no keywords doesn't.
🏷
Front-load the first line
The first sentence of your caption carries the most search and scroll-stopping weight. Lead with the clearest, most specific version of what the post is about, not a vague hook designed only for suspense.
🖼
Use alt text on purpose
Alt text exists for accessibility first, and it also feeds the algorithm information about your content. Write a genuine, descriptive line about the image instead of leaving it blank or keyword-stuffing it. It helps real people and helps your discoverability at the same time.
#️⃣
A few specific hashtags, not thirty generic ones
Three to five specific, relevant hashtags do more than a maxed-out list of broad ones. Specific niche hashtags get you in front of the right small audience. Broad hashtags get you lost in an ocean of unrelated content.
Why community matters more than reach
🫂
A smaller, real audience outperforms a bigger, quiet one
A thousand people who comment, reply to your Stories, and actually buy from or refer you matter more than ten thousand who scroll past silently. Coming back is a good moment to stop chasing reach and start nurturing the people who are already there.
📩
DMs and Story replies are where relationships actually form
Public posts get people to notice you. Private replies are where they decide to trust you. If you only have energy for one type of engagement this week, make it the DMs and Story replies you've let pile up.
🤝
Show up in other people's comments, not just your own
Commenting thoughtfully on a handful of accounts in your niche puts you back in front of new people without making a single new post. It rebuilds visibility and relationships at the same time, and it's far less draining than producing content from nothing.
A mindful, low-overwhelm way to actually begin
✦
Start here, not with a strategy document
You do not need a full content calendar, a rebrand, or a niche overhaul before you're "allowed" to post again. Open the app, write one honest sentence about anything, and let that be today's win. Strategy can come in week two. Momentum has to come first.
🪶
Pick one small action, not a five-step plan
Today's task is not "fix my Instagram." Today's task is "reply to three comments" or "post one Story." A five-step relaunch plan sounds productive and usually becomes another reason to stall. One small, finishable action moves you forward today.
📓
Brain dump before you draft
Open a Notebook and write down everything you've wanted to say but haven't, with no structure or editing. You're not writing a post yet. You're clearing the backlog in your head so the actual posting feels lighter.
🗓
Give yourself a real, lower bar
Define what "back" means for you specifically: maybe it's two posts a week for a month, not daily content forever. Write that number down somewhere you'll see it, so the goal you're working toward is one you actually set, not one you assumed you needed.
🌤
Expect a quiet stretch to happen again, and plan for it
ND brains go through natural cycles of output and rest. Treat the next quiet stretch as expected maintenance, not failure. The goal isn't to never go quiet again. It's to make coming back easier and less loaded every time it happens.
Six things to remember when you're coming back
  • 🌱
    The gap is smaller in other people's eyes than it is in yours. Most followers were not tracking your absence the way you were. You're allowed to just start posting again.
  • ◎
    Engagement is a habit you rebuild, not a switch you flip. Ten minutes of replying and commenting most days will rebuild your presence faster than one big content push.
  • ✶
    Searchable captions matter more than hashtag volume now. Write like your ideal audience is typing into the search bar, because increasingly, they are.
  • ✦
    A smaller, real community beats a bigger, silent one. Coming back is a good time to nurture the people already there instead of chasing new reach.
  • ◎
    Pick the lowest-effort format for your first post back. Momentum matters more than polish when you're just getting started again.
  • ✶
    Quiet stretches will happen again, and that's allowed. The goal is a softer landing next time, not permanent, unbroken consistency.
← Back to Guides
🧠
Big Brain Energy (Strategy Edition)
Content without strategy is a guess. Strategy without content is a deck nobody reads.
This is the strategist side of your Creative Director. When to send, how often to post, what to actually focus on this week, ask and get a real answer instead of a shrug.
Why this isn't as intimidating as it sounds
Strategy is just a decision you made on purpose instead of by accident.
A lot of entrepreneurs hear "strategy" and picture a spreadsheet, a funnel diagram, a quarterly planning meeting that sounds exhausting before it even starts. That's not what this is. Strategy is just the difference between posting because it's Tuesday and posting because Tuesday is actually when your people show up. It's the difference between launching because the date felt right and launching because you built in enough runway. You're already making these decisions. The only question is whether you're making them on purpose or by accident, tired, at 11pm, hoping it works out.
🧭
You don't need to become a different kind of person
You don't have to turn into a spreadsheet-and-KPI person to think strategically. You just need a place to ask "does this make sense" before you commit time to it, and an honest answer back. That's the whole job of this layer.
⏳
It's allowed to feel small at first
You don't have to overhaul your whole approach in one sitting. The first useful strategy conversation might just be "should this be a newsletter or a post." Start there. The bigger questions get easier once asking feels normal.
What to actually ask Director Chat
🧠
The Studio move for this
Open Director Chat and ask it a real logistics question, not just a writing one. It now has a Strategy & Logistics profile (Settings) it can pull from, your platforms, your posting frequency, your audience's timezone, your current goal, and anything you've told it about what's worked before. The more of that you fill in, the more specific its answers get.
📬
"When should I send my newsletter this week?"
It'll give you an actual day and a reason, not a shrug. If you've told it what's worked before, it'll weigh that over generic best practice.
📊
"How often should I realistically be posting right now?"
Give it your current phase or goal and it'll reason from that, not from some universal "post daily" rule that doesn't account for your capacity or your launch window.
🚀
"I'm launching in three weeks, what should my content look like leading up to it?"
This is launch pacing. It can map out a rough sequence, awareness, anticipation, doors open, last call, instead of you guessing how early is too early.
🪜
"What should I actually prioritize this week?"
When everything feels equally urgent, this question forces a real answer instead of you defaulting to whatever's loudest in your head.
Questions worth sitting with before you ask
A strategist's first move is always a few honest questions, not an immediate answer.
Before you open the chat, it can help to ask yourself a couple of these. You don't need polished answers, just whatever's true right now. What's actually pulling at your attention this week, the content or the logistics behind it. Where do you feel busy but not sure it's adding up to anything. What's one thing that's worked before that you've never actually written down anywhere. The Studio can reason a lot better with a real answer to "what's worked before" than with silence, so this is worth a few honest minutes.
Setting up the Strategy & Logistics profile
📍
Platforms and frequency
Even a rough answer helps. "Instagram, 3 times a week, plus a weekly newsletter" gives the Studio something real to reason from instead of guessing what you're actually managing.
🌍
Audience timezone
If your people are mostly in one timezone, say so. If you're split across a few, that's useful too. Timing advice only works if it knows who it's timing for.
🎯
Current phase or goal
Are you in growth mode, nurturing your current audience, mid-launch, or just trying to stay consistent without burning out. This one field changes almost every strategic answer you'll get.
📈
What's worked before
This is the field that turns generic advice into your advice. "Newsletter opens are always better on Tuesdays" or "carousels do better than reels for me" outweighs any general rule the Studio would otherwise default to.
Easing into strategy as an ND entrepreneur
✦
Start with one question, not a system
You don't need a content strategy document before you're allowed to ask a strategic question. Pick one decision you're actually facing this week and ask Director Chat about that single thing. Strategy as a habit gets built one real decision at a time, not by sitting down to plan everything at once.
🌀
Executive function and strategy aren't opposites
Strategic thinking often gets framed as the opposite of an ND brain's natural pace, all planning and no flow. In practice, having a strategist available on demand removes decisions from your plate instead of adding to it. You're not doing more thinking. You're outsourcing the part that used to drain you.
🪶
You're allowed to disagree with it
A real strategist gives you a recommendation, not an order. If Director Chat suggests a timeline or a cadence that doesn't fit your life, say so and ask for an alternative. The goal is a second opinion you trust, not a rule you have to follow.
🔁
Strategy is allowed to change as often as you need it to
What made sense last month doesn't have to still make sense this month. Update your Strategy & Logistics profile whenever your goal shifts. A launch month and a quiet, sustainable month should not be getting the same advice.
💬
Think out loud, it's built for that too
You don't need a clean question. "I don't know if I should post about the launch yet or wait" is a perfectly good thing to type exactly as messy as it is in your head. Director Chat can work with that.
Six things to remember about the strategy layer
  • ◈
    A real answer beats a safe non-answer. If Director Chat ever shrugs back at you with "whenever works for you," push it. Ask it to commit to a specific recommendation and tell you why.
  • ✦
    Fill out the Strategy & Logistics profile once, then forget about it. It quietly upgrades every strategic answer you get from here on out, no extra effort per conversation.
  • ◎
    "What's worked before" is your strongest lever. One honest sentence about your own results outweighs general platform advice every time.
  • ✶
    Strategy questions don't need to be big to be worth asking. "Should this be a post or a newsletter" is a strategy question. Start there.
  • ◈
    You can disagree with the recommendation. It's a second opinion, not a directive. Push back if something doesn't fit your actual life.
  • ◎
    Update your goal field as it changes. Launch-month strategy and maintenance-month strategy should look different. Keep that field current.
